title: Python module batch C: functions, basic error handling (2 lessons + exercises)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). Functions and error handling complete the Python beginner module's core concepts. Functions are the most important abstraction a beginner learns; error handling teaches defensive, safe programming practice. Both lessons complete the ≈ 8–10 lesson Python module needed for M1 Definition of Done.
objective: Author two Python beginner lessons covering functions (def, parameters, return, scope) and basic error handling (try/except, common exceptions, reading error messages) — each with original prose, at least one runnable example, and at least one graded exercise.
acceptanceCriteria: Two lessons are delivered: (1) functions (def, parameters with defaults, return values, basic scope), (2) error handling (try/except, ValueError/TypeError/IndexError, reading tracebacks).
Every lesson has at least 1 runnable example and at least 1 graded exercise with solutionVerified:true and starter code that does NOT pass the tests.
All prose is original; at least 2 authoritative cited sources per lesson; no copied prose.
Each lesson is schema-valid; technical + pedagogy review by non-authors.
Examples are neutral/inclusive; prerequisites (batch A and B) are honestly stated.
output: Two merged lesson documents (with exercise files) for functions and basic error handling in Python, each schema-valid, correctness-verified, and reviewed.
